mn109:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in the Eastern Park, in the palace of Migāra’s Mother.
mn109:2.1: Now on that occasion, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, on the night of the full moon,[^1] the Blessed One was sitting in the open, surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
mn109:3.1: Then a certain bhikkhu rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One, and said to the Blessed One:
mn109:3.2: “Venerable sir, I would ask the Blessed One about a certain point, if the Blessed One would grant me the favour of answering my question.”
mn109:3.3: “Well then, bhikkhu, sit down on your own seat and ask what you like.”
mn109:3.4: Then that bhikkhu sat down on his own seat and said to the Blessed One:
mn109:4.1: “Venerable sir, are there these five aggregates affected by clinging, that is to say,
mn109:4.2: the form aggregate affected by clinging, the feeling aggregate affected by clinging, the perception aggregate affected by clinging, the formations aggregate affected by clinging, the consciousness aggregate affected by clinging?”
mn109:4.3: “There are, bhikkhu, these five aggregates affected by clinging, that is to say,
mn109:4.4: the form aggregate affected by clinging, the feeling aggregate affected by clinging, the perception aggregate affected by clinging, the formations aggregate affected by clinging, the consciousness aggregate affected by clinging.”
mn109:4.5: Saying, “Good, venerable sir,” that bhikkhu delighted in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, and he asked the Blessed One a further question:
mn109:5.1: “But, venerable sir, what are these five aggregates affected by clinging rooted in?”
mn109:5.2: “These five aggregates affected by clinging, bhikkhu, are rooted in desire.”
mn109:6.1: “Venerable sir, is that clinging the same as these five aggregates affected by clinging, or is the clinging something apart from the five aggregates affected by clinging?”
mn109:6.2: “Bhikkhu, that clinging is neither the same as these five aggregates affected by clinging, nor is it something apart from the five aggregates affected by clinging.
mn109:6.3: It is the desire and lust comprised in these five aggregates affected by clinging that is the clinging there.”
mn109:7.1: “But, venerable sir, might there be diversity in the desire and lust comprised in these five aggregates affected by clinging?”
mn109:7.2: “There might, bhikkhu,” the Blessed One said.
mn109:7.4: ‘May my form be such in the future; may my feeling be such in the future; may my perception be such in the future; may my formations be such in the future; may my consciousness be such in the future.’
mn109:7.5: Thus, bhikkhu, there is diversity in the desire and lust comprised in these five aggregates affected by clinging.”
mn109:8.1: “But, venerable sir, in what way is ‘aggregate’ a term for the aggregates?”
mn109:8.2: “Whatever kind of form there is, bhikkhu—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the form aggregate.
mn109:8.3: Whatever kind of feeling there is—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the feeling aggregate.
mn109:8.4: Whatever kind of perception there is—past, future or present …—this is called the perception aggregate.
mn109:8.5: Whatever kind of formations there are—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the formations aggregate.
mn109:8.6: Whatever kind of consciousness there is—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the consciousness aggregate.
mn109:8.7: It is in this way, bhikkhu, that ‘aggregate’ is a term for the aggregates.”
mn109:9.1: “What is the reason, venerable sir, what is the condition, for describing the form aggregate?
mn109:9.2: What is the reason, what is the condition, for describing the feeling aggregate?
mn109:9.3: What is the reason, what is the condition, for describing the perception aggregate?
mn109:9.4: What is the reason, what is the condition, for describing the formations aggregate?
mn109:9.5: What is the reason, what is the condition, for describing the consciousness aggregate?”
mn109:9.6: “The four great primary elements, bhikkhu, are the reason, the four great primary elements are the condition, for describing the form aggregate.
mn109:9.7: Contact is the reason, contact is the condition, for describing the feeling aggregate.
mn109:9.8: Contact is the reason, contact is the condition, for describing the perception aggregate.
mn109:9.9: Contact is the reason, contact is the condition, for describing the formations aggregate.
mn109:9.10: Name-and-form is the reason, bhikkhu, name-and-form is the condition, for describing the consciousness aggregate.”
mn109:10.1: “But, venerable sir, how does there come to be the embodiment view?”
mn109:10.2: “Here, bhikkhu, the untaught ordinary man, who has no regard for the Noble Ones and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it, who has no regard for True Men and is unconversant with their Dhamma and undisciplined in it,
mn109:10.3: sees form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;
mn109:10.4: he sees feeling as self, or self as possessed of feeling, or feeling in self, or self in feeling;
mn109:10.5: he sees perception as self, or self as possessed of perception, or perception in self, or self in perception;
mn109:10.6: he sees formations as self, or self as possessed of formations, or formations in self, or self in formations;
mn109:10.7: he sees consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.
mn109:10.8: That, bhikkhu, is how there comes to be the embodiment view.”
mn109:11.1: “But, venerable sir, how does there not come to be the embodiment view?”
mn109:11.2: “Here, bhikkhu, the well-taught noble disciple, who has regard for the Noble Ones and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it, who has regard for True Men and is conversant with their Dhamma and disciplined in it,
mn109:11.3: does not see form as self, or self as possessed of form, or form in self, or self in form;
mn109:11.4: he does not see feeling as self, or self as possessed of feeling, or feeling in self, or self in feeling;
mn109:11.5: he does not see perception as self, or self as possessed of perception, or perception in self, or self in perception;
mn109:11.6: he does not see formations as self, or self as possessed of formations, or formations in self, or self in formations;
mn109:11.7: he does not see consciousness as self, or self as possessed of consciousness, or consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.
mn109:11.8: That, bhikkhu, is how there does not come to be the embodiment view.”
mn109:12.1: “What is the gratification, venerable sir, what is the danger, what is the escape,[^2] in the case of form?
mn109:12.2: What is the gratification, what is the danger, what is the escape, in the case of feeling?
mn109:12.3: What is the gratification, what is the danger, what is the escape, in the case of perception?
mn109:12.4: What is the gratification, what is the danger, what is the escape, in the case of formations?
mn109:12.5: What is the gratification, what is the danger, what is the escape, in the case of consciousness?”
mn109:12.6: “The pleasure and joy, bhikkhu, that arise dependent on form—this is the gratification in the case of form.
mn109:12.7: Form is impermanent, painful, and subject to change—this is the danger in the case of form.
mn109:12.8: The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust, for form—this is the escape in the case of form.
mn109:12.9: The pleasure and joy that arise dependent on feeling …
mn109:12.12: the pleasure and joy that arise dependent on consciousness—this is the gratification in the case of consciousness.
mn109:12.13: Consciousness is impermanent, painful, and subject to change—this is the danger in the case of consciousness.
mn109:12.14: The removal of desire and lust, the abandonment of desire and lust, for consciousness—this is the escape in the case of consciousness.”
mn109:13.1: “But, venerable sir, how does a man know, how does he see, so that there come to be in him, in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external signs, no underlying tendency to I-making, mine-making and conceit?”
mn109:13.2: “Whatever kind of form there is, bhikkhu—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—he sees all form as it actually is with right understanding thus: ‘This is not mine, this is not I, this is not my self.’
mn109:13.3: Whatever kind of feeling there is …
mn109:13.4: whatever kind of perception there is …
mn109:13.5: whatever kind of formations there are …
mn109:13.6: whatever kind of consciousness there is—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—he sees all consciousness as it actually is with right understanding thus: ‘This is not mine, this is not I, this is not my self.’
mn109:13.7: That, bhikkhu, is how a man knows, how he sees, so that there come to be in him, in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external signs, no underlying tendency to I-making, mine-making and conceit.”
mn109:14.1: Then a thought arose in the mind of a certain bhikkhu:
mn109:14.2: “So, it seems, form is not self, feeling is not self, perception is not self, formations are not self, consciousness is not self.
mn109:14.3: Then what self will actions done by what is not self affect?”[^3]
mn109:14.4: Then the Blessed One, knowing in his own mind the thought in that bhikkhu’s mind, addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn109:14.5: “It is possible, bhikkhus, that some misguided man here, unknowing and ignorant, with his mind dominated by craving, might think he could outstrip the Teacher’s Dispensation thus:
mn109:14.6: ‘So, it seems, form is not self, feeling is not self, perception is not self, formations are not self, consciousness is not self.
mn109:14.7: Then what self will actions done by what is not self affect?’
mn109:14.8: Now, bhikkhus, you have been trained by me through questioning about these various matters here and there in the Dhamma.
mn109:15.1: How do you conceive this, bhikkhus,
mn109:15.4: “And is what is impermanent painful or pleasant?”
mn109:15.6: “And is what is impermanent, painful, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
mn109:15.7: ‘This is mine, this is I, this is my self’?”
mn109:16.7: “And is what is impermanent painful or pleasant?”
mn109:16.9: “And is what is impermanent, painful, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
mn109:16.10: ‘This is mine, this is I, this is my self’?”
mn109:16.12: “Therefore, bhikkhus, whatever kind of form there is—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form should be seen as it actually is with right understanding thus: ‘This is not mine, this is not I, this is not my self.’
mn109:17.1: Whatever kind of feeling there is …
mn109:17.2: whatever kind of perception there is …
mn109:17.3: whatever kind of formations there are …
mn109:17.4: whatever kind of consciousness there is—past, future or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all consciousness should be seen as it actually is with right understanding thus: ‘This is not mine, this is not I, this is not my self.’
mn109:17.5: Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the well-taught noble disciple becomes dispassionate towards form, dispassionate towards feeling, dispassionate towards perception, dispassionate towards formations, dispassionate towards consciousness.
mn109:18.1: Being dispassionate, his greed fades away; with the fading of greed his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It is liberated.’
mn109:18.2: He understands: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’”
mn109:18.3: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn109:18.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
mn109:18.5: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of as many as sixty bhikkhus were liberated from the taints by not clinging.
